name: Capacitor-Grade BOPP/Dielectric Films
scope: Ultra-thin metallised BOPP/PET dielectric film for film capacitors (EV inverters and chargers, solar/wind inverters, grid capacitor banks, drives) and the Indian listed companies making, metallising, buying or adjacent to it.

summary.one_line: Polypropylene film made it into the latest ECMS round, and Xpro India confirmed that some key customers have approved its 3.5-micron ultra-thin grade. Jindal Poly swung to an Rs 85 cr Q2 loss with a qualified consolidated review, and signed a 12-day standstill in the JPFL Films dispute.
key_points: ECMS, 6 Nov 2026: the government approved 12 more applications worth Rs 7,503 cr, and polypropylene film is among the listed products. No company is named. The cumulative total is now 118 approvals and Rs 77,051 cr of investment (S24).

Xpro India, 9 Nov investor meet: dielectric-film revenue rose 64% YoY in Q2, and dielectric exports nearly doubled. Some key customers have approved its 3.5-micron ultra-thin film, while 1,000-2,000 hour life tests continue at others. Indicative prices are about Rs 470-480/kg for conventional film and just above Rs 600/kg for 3.5 micron. The UAE line is expected to start commercial operations later in FY27 (S25). A postal ballot seeks approval for Rs 370 cr of transactions with the UAE subsidiary (S16).

Jindal Poly, Q2 FY27 (14 Nov): revenue was Rs 738 cr (+26.5% YoY) with a consolidated net loss of about Rs 85-86 cr (S18, S22). The consolidated review is qualified, because inventory at the subsidiary hit by the May 2025 Nashik fire has not been verified. The standalone loss of Rs 350 cr includes a Rs 292 cr provision against a loan to a subsidiary (S18).

On 13 Nov, Jindal Poly, JPFL Films and Brookfield-affiliated Project Holdings Fourteen agreed a 12-day standstill on all pending proceedings to explore a settlement. It lapses around 25 Nov unless extended. The investor holds about 38% of JPFL's paid-up capital (S23).

Cosmo First: there is no new capacitor-film disclosure, and its website still calls the second metalliser forthcoming (S3). On 18 Nov it disclosed a Maharashtra GST inspection and search at its Aurangabad units (S12).

Market size (unchanged): QYResearch puts global capacitor-grade BOPP at USD 874.5 mn in 2025, reaching USD 1,336.2 mn by 2032 (6.25% CAGR) (S17). IndexBox sees 6-9% annual growth over 2026-35, with EV power electronics at 10-14% (S1).
Prices, 4 to 18 Nov 2026: Xpro rose 14.4% to 84x P/E; Cosmo rose 3.8%, Jindal Poly fell 4.9% and SRF rose 0.7%. All four remain 17-35% below their 52-week highs (S12, S13, S14, S16).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Xpro India has the most direct exposure: dielectric film made up Rs 135.52 cr of FY26 sales (S15), and dielectric revenue grew 64% YoY in Q2 (S25). Approval of its 3.5-micron grade opens the higher-priced end of the range, at above Rs 600/kg versus Rs 470-480/kg for conventional film (S25). At 84x P/E (S16), the market already prices in a lot of this.
Metallisers and capacitor makers approved under ECMS, plus any company approved for polypropylene film, add domestic demand for base film (S10, S24).
SRF has run a capacitor-grade BOPP plant at Indore since 15 May 2026, at about Rs 277 cr (S9). The business is small within group sales of Rs 18,265 cr (S14).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Jindal Poly: Q2 swung to a loss with a qualified consolidated review (S18), and the JPFL shareholder dispute is only paused, not settled (S23). The SEBI show-cause notice is still open (S6), and CRISIL's latest rationale we found has the ratings on Watch Negative (S7).
Qualification is slow. Xpro's approvals turn into volume only after 1,000-2,000 hour life tests, and costs from the new line weigh on margins until utilisation rises (S25).

Domestic capacity is rising at SRF, Xpro (Barjora plus UAE) and JPFL (5,000 TPA per CRISIL), and now through ECMS-backed polypropylene film (S7, S9, S24, S25). No source we could verify quantifies Indian demand.
Polypropylene is 50-65% of production cost, and China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Jindal Poly: whether the 13 Nov standstill is extended or turns into a settlement, and whether the Rs 292 cr loan dispute is resolved (S18, S23).
Xpro: commercial start of the UAE line later in FY27, the postal-ballot result, and further ultra-thin grade approvals (S16, S25).
Which company holds the ECMS polypropylene-film approval in the 6 Nov round (S24).
Cosmo: the outcome of the GST search, and any start-up of the second metalliser (S3, S12).
Finance Ministry notification of DGTR's PET-film anti-dumping recommendation; the case does not cover BOPP (S8).

blocks.text: Capacitor-grade film is an ultra-thin dielectric film, the insulating layer between a capacitor's plates. It is mostly biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP), vacuum-metallised with aluminium or aluminium-zinc and wound into film capacitors. Cosmo First makes it at 2.5-12 micron, in clean-room conditions with micro-slitting, for AC and DC capacitors (S2). Xpro India makes 2-16 micron base film for power capacitors, EV systems and railways (S15). Packaging BOPP is thicker and has no comparable purity or surface requirements. The thin metal layer lets the capacitor 'self-heal': a local short burns the metal away instead of destroying the part.

Demand is moving to thinner films with higher breakdown voltage. IndexBox sees EV demand shifting to 2-4 micron BOPP. It expects BOPP to keep 60-70% of volume, with metallised film at 40-50% of value (S1). Prices rise steeply as films get thinner. At its 9 Nov investor meet, Xpro gave these indicative prices (S25):

items: Conventional film: about Rs 470-480/kg.
3.5 micron: slightly above Rs 600/kg.
3 micron: possibly close to Rs 900/kg.

blocks.text: Xpro also said conventional dielectric margins range from roughly 35% to 55%, depending on film type (S25).
Cosmo's metallised grades show the range of end uses (S3):

items: Al-Zn standard: fans and motor-run capacitors.
Slope/RMF: APFC panels and wind.
Segmented: power supplies.
'Series': variable-frequency drives, renewable inverters, UPS and EVs.

blocks.text: Xpro names EV inverters, solar and wind, grid equipment, railways and data centres as end markets (S25).

blocks.caption: Third-party forecasts (each is the publisher's own forecast)

blocks.title: Global capacitor-grade BOPP film market (QYResearch forecast)

blocks.text: The two forecasts agree on mid-to-high single-digit growth. QYResearch names Xpro India and the B.C. Jindal group among global suppliers, alongside Toray, Oji, Shin-Etsu, Bolloré, Tervakoski and Chinese producers (S17). We did not verify Mordor and FMI figures, so they are left out. We found no verified figure for the size of the Indian market.

When Cosmo launched capacitor film in Dec 2023, it said the product was largely imported from China, and saw room for import substitution and exports (S2). China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1). We found no official tonnage series for India's capacitor-film imports.

DGTR has recommended anti-dumping duties on PET film from Bangladesh, China and Thailand (S8). As of 19 Nov we found no Finance Ministry notification. The case covers PET film, not BOPP, the main capacitor dielectric (S1). We found no capacitor-BOPP-specific trade action.

subsections.title: Confirmed producers: what changed in the past two weeks

blocks.text: Xpro India: on 9 Nov, management said dielectric-film revenue rose 64% YoY in Q2 and dielectric exports nearly doubled. Barjora output rose 35% QoQ (S25). Customer qualification has moved forward:

items: Some key customers have approved the 3.5-micron ultra-thin film (S25).
Other customers are still running 1,000-2,000 hour capacitor life tests, and volumes follow only after those tests (S25).

blocks.text: Management said Xpro is on track to exceed Rs 700 cr of FY27 revenue if current market conditions hold, and called this conditional, not firm guidance (S25). The UAE line has all key equipment installed and is expected to start commercial operations later in FY27. Management flagged the regional conflict as a risk (S25). A 13 Nov postal ballot seeks approval for Rs 370 cr of transactions with the UAE subsidiary, including a Rs 220 cr guarantee and a Rs 60 cr loan (S16).
Jindal Poly Films, Q2 FY27 (filed 14 Nov):

items: Revenue was Rs 738.1 cr, up 26.5% YoY from Rs 583.4 cr (S18). One aggregator gives a Rs 410 cr year-ago base, presumably on a different restatement; we use the Rs 583 cr figure, which matches Screener (S13).
Consolidated net loss was Rs 85.2 cr (S18), or Rs 86.17 cr in a second summary (S22), against a Rs 107 cr profit in Q1. It included a Rs 96.43 cr loss on fair valuation of investments (S22).
The packaging-films segment lost Rs 25.66 cr on revenue of Rs 430.64 cr (S22).

blocks.text: Jindal Poly's consolidated limited review is qualified: the auditor could not verify inventory at the subsidiary hit by the fire (S18). That fire was at the Nashik plant on 21 May 2025, and the subsidiary's inventory is carried at Rs 277.74 cr (S22). The standalone loss of Rs 350 cr includes a Rs 292 cr provision against a loan to a subsidiary (S18). The investor-shareholder says that loan breached a reserved matter under the 16 Mar 2022 shareholders' agreement, the subject of the 16 Oct arbitration notice (S21, S22). On 13 Nov the parties signed a 12-day standstill of all proceedings to explore a settlement. No money changes hands under it (S23).

Cosmo First: there was no new capacitor-film disclosure this fortnight. The Q2 FY27 release covers specialty chemicals, coated films and Plastech, and does not mention capacitor film (S19). On 18 Nov the company disclosed a Maharashtra GST inspection and search at its Aurangabad units (S12).
SRF: the Indore capacitor-grade BOPP plant has been running since 15 May 2026 (S9). Its November exchange filings on Screener are SAST disclosures with no capacitor-film content (S14).

Only Xpro India reports capacitor-film revenue: Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT in FY26 (S15), plus the Q2 growth rate (S25). Any capacitor-film share for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly would be an estimate, so none is given.

items: Pan Electronics (India), BSE 517397: a Bengaluru micro-cap that has metallised polypropylene and polyester dielectric films since 1986 and has moved into MPP capacitors (S11). It is immaterial in size.
Universal Cables makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels, so it is a potential domestic film buyer (S5). No film-supply tie-up has been disclosed.
Polyplex and UFlex (Flex Films): IndexBox lists both among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1), but we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade. Both stay in 'other'.

blocks.text: Coverage gap: India's main film-capacitor makers (e.g. TDK India, Vishay India) are unlisted subsidiaries, and the 6 Nov ECMS polypropylene-film applicant is unnamed (S24). The listed exposure is therefore:

items: Small caps: Xpro, Cosmo and Jindal Poly.
A micro-cap metalliser: Pan Electronics.
A large cap where capacitor film is a small business: SRF.

blocks.text: We found no mid-cap pure play.

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.title: Share price change, 4 Nov to 18 Nov 2026
blocks.source: Source: Screener.in (S12, S13, S14, S16); 4 Nov prices from the W45 edition

blocks.text: Xpro, the only producer that discloses large capacitor-film exposure, keeps re-rating. It is up another 14% since 4 Nov, to 84x trailing P/E (S16), after its investor meet on ultra-thin approvals and pricing (S25). Cosmo is at 9.7x (S12), so the market gives little value to its capacitor line. Jindal Poly trades below book, at 0.94x, given the loss and the dispute (S13). SRF is a large cap valued on chemicals; capacitor film is too small to move the stock (S14). All four are trading 17-35% below their 52-week highs (S12, S13, S14, S16). We could not confirm 6- and 12-month returns from a source we opened, so they are left out.

Coverage remains thin. The results coverage of Xpro comes mainly from aggregators summarising its filings and call (S20, S25), and Jindal Poly's results coverage does not mention capacitor film (S18, S22). We found no Indian broker note or mainstream-media piece built around capacitor film.

items: Resin cost: polypropylene is 50-65% of production cost (S1).
Chinese overcapacity: China holds 35-45% of global capacity (S1), and India's imports came mostly from China (S2).
Qualification lag: Xpro's volumes follow only after 1,000-2,000 hour life tests, and new-line costs weigh on margins until utilisation rises (S25).
Execution at Xpro's UAE plant: management flags the regional conflict as a risk to logistics and cost, and the plant needs Rs 370 cr of parent support (S16, S25).
Domestic supply build-out: SRF (S9), Xpro (S25), JPFL at 5,000 TPA (S7) and the ECMS polypropylene-film approval (S24). We found no verified figure for Indian demand.
Small share of revenue: capacitor film is not material in Cosmo's or SRF's reported drivers (S14, S19).

Governance at Jindal Poly: a qualified consolidated review and a Rs 292 cr loan provision (S18), the JPFL shareholder dispute, paused but not resolved (S23), the open SEBI notice (S6) and CRISIL's Watch Negative (S7).
Cosmo: the outcome of the 18 Nov GST search is unknown (S12).
Commercial start of Xpro's UAE line, and further customer approvals of its ultra-thin grades (S25).
Expiry, extension or settlement of the JPFL standstill around 25 Nov (S23); confirmation of JPFL's capacitor-film doubling (S4, S7).
Naming of the 6 Nov ECMS polypropylene-film applicant, and any further ECMS rounds (S24).
Cosmo's second metalliser coming on stream (S3).
Localisation of EV and solar inverters, the segment IndexBox expects to grow 10-14% a year (S1).
Notification of the PET-film anti-dumping duty (S8). No trade action specific to capacitor BOPP has been found.

companies.name: Xpro India Ltd
companies.role: Dedicated BOPP dielectric base-film maker at Barjora (2-16 micron). FY26 dielectric sales were Rs 135.52 cr on 3,541 MT (S15), and India capacity is 8,000 MT/yr after the Barjora line, with a third line in the UAE (S25). QYResearch names it among global players (S17).
companies.impact: Dielectric revenue rose 64% YoY in Q2, and some key customers have approved its 3.5-micron grade, which sells for more than Rs 600/kg (S25). At 84x P/E (S16), execution on the UAE line and life-test approvals has to keep pace.

companies.name: SRF Ltd
companies.role: Commissioned phase 1 of its Indore capacitor-grade BOPP plant on 15 May 2026 at about Rs 277 cr (S9). Holds an ECMS approval for a Rs 496 cr capacitor PP-film project (S10).
companies.impact: The fastest-scaling domestic competitor to Xpro and Cosmo, but small within Rs 18,265 cr of group sales (S14).

companies.name: Cosmo First Ltd
companies.role: Makes metallised capacitor-grade BOPP, launched in Dec 2023 at ~750 MT/yr in 2.5-12 micron (S2). The metalliser is now rated 900 MT/yr, with a second forthcoming (S3).
companies.impact: Capacitor film does not feature in Q2 FY27 drivers (S19). Trades at 9.7x P/E, and an 18 Nov GST search at its Aurangabad units is a new overhang (S12).

companies.name: Jindal Poly Films Ltd
companies.role: Its subsidiary JPFL Films makes capacitor film: 5,000 TPA is operational per CRISIL (S7), and a Rs 250 cr doubling was announced in 2024 (S4). QYResearch lists the B.C. Jindal group among global players (S17).
companies.impact: Q2 FY27 loss of about Rs 85 cr with a qualified consolidated review (S18). The JPFL dispute with Brookfield's affiliate is paused under a 12-day standstill (S23), and the SEBI notice is still open (S6). Governance outweighs the capacitor theme.

companies.name: Pan Electronics (India) Ltd
companies.role: Bengaluru micro-cap that metallises polypropylene and polyester dielectric films (since 1986) and now makes MPP capacitors (S11).
companies.impact: A potential buyer of domestic base film, but immaterial in investment terms given its tiny size (S11).

companies.name: Universal Cables Ltd
companies.role: Makes all-polypropylene LT/HT power capacitors and APFC panels (S5).
companies.impact: A potential domestic film buyer as local supply grows. No film-supply tie-up has been disclosed (S5).

companies.name: Polyplex Corporation Ltd
companies.role: BOPET film maker that IndexBox lists among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: no company-confirmed capacitor grade. The PET-film anti-dumping case is more relevant to it (S8).

companies.name: UFlex Ltd
companies.role: Its Flex Films business makes BOPP/BOPET films; IndexBox lists it among Indian dielectric-film producers (S1).
companies.impact: Adjacent only: we found no company-confirmed capacitor grade (S1).

method:
Refresh of the 2026-W45 edition (5 Nov), researched on 19 Nov 2026 with web search and page fetches.

New this edition:
- Jindal Poly's Q2 FY27 results, from two aggregator summaries of the filing (S18, S22) cross-checked against Screener (S13). The sources give different net-loss figures (Rs 85.2 cr and Rs 86.17 cr), and both are shown. A third summary gives a Rs 410 cr year-ago revenue base; it was not used because Screener shows Rs 583 cr.
- The 13 Nov JPFL standstill, from the NSE filing as seen in search results; the PDF itself timed out on fetch (S23).
- The 6 Nov ECMS round (S24), cross-checked against ThePrint and IBEF. None of these name the polypropylene-film applicant.
- Xpro's 9 Nov investor-meet commentary (S25) and its 13 Nov postal ballot (S16).
- Cosmo's 18 Nov GST-search disclosure (S12).

Prices: Screener closes for 18 Nov, fetched 19 Nov. Changes are measured against the 4 Nov closes in the W45 edition.

Searches found:
- No CRISIL action after May 2026 that we could open; Screener lists a 12 Nov CRISIL update, but its content was not seen.
- No Finance Ministry notification of the PET-film anti-dumping duty.
- No new SRF capacitor-film announcement.
- No start-up of Cosmo's second metalliser.

Dropped as stale or to keep to 25 sources:
- The 13,000 MT Xpro target (FilingReader).
- The Aug 2026 ECMS tranche detail, including Capfilm, and the Mar 2026 Dhruv/Vishay approvals.
- SRF's Q2 call commentary on a second line and premium pricing.

Carried over without re-opening: IndexBox, QYResearch, CRISIL May 2026, the PET anti-dumping article and the company profile pages.

Not stated because not confirmed: capacitor-film revenue for SRF, Cosmo or Jindal Poly, Indian import tonnage or market size, and 6- and 12-month returns.

No ratings or price targets are given.
